sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Abilene, TX?
sections.html:
For Abilene homes in Taylor County, the bill comes from the Central Appraisal District of Taylor County, because the county's own tax assessor-collector office does not collect property taxes. The Texas Comptroller's county directory says so directly and points owners to the appraisal district.

That one bill covers every local unit on your parcel. The directory lists Taylor County, the City of Abilene, Abilene Independent School District and a handful of other cities and school districts among the active taxing units, and the district office is at 1534 S. Treadaway Blvd., phone 325-676-9381, open weekdays 8 AM to 5 PM.

  • The online portal, run by Point and Pay, adds a convenience fee: 2.3 percent on credit cards (minimum $2.00), $3.00 flat on Visa debit, and $1.00 on an e-check.
  • Card payments take four to five business days to post, although the date you pay is used as the payment date.
  • Escrow companies and multiple-property owners have their own payment links on the district's pay page.

sections.h2: What is the Abilene city property tax rate?
sections.html:
Abilene's council set the city rate at 74.95 cents per $100 of taxable value, a little below the previous 75.06 cents. It adopted a $414.6 million operating budget on September 10, 2026, and the fiscal year began October 1.

A lower rate did not mean a lower bill for most owners. The city's own release estimates an average 4.2 percent tax increase on existing property because values rose, and says new property accounts for $16.8 million of the $18.3 million increase in property tax revenue. The city also counted one more figure: in its budget presentation, a homestead with the median taxable value saw that value move from $163,456 to $171,775 and the city bill go from $1,226.90 to $1,287.45.

sections.h2: When is the Abilene tax bill due, and what happens if it is late?
sections.html:
Bills go out around October 1, and the Comptroller says most owners must pay by January 31. Anything unpaid on February 1 is delinquent, and the collector adds a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest that day.

The penalty then grows 1 percent each month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent. Interest keeps running at 1 percent a month with no cap. A taxing unit with an attorney contract may add as much as 20 percent. Owners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans may pay a homestead bill in installments, and some collectors offer plans of up to 36 months on a residence homestead.

  • A waiver of penalty and interest usually requires payment within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and a written request before the 181st day after the delinquency date.
  • An owner who appeals must generally pay the undisputed amount before delinquency.
  • A bill mailed late in January can move the delinquency date to the first of a later month, but never gives less than 21 days.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower an Abilene bill?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption is the big one. Abilene ISD must take $140,000 off a homestead's value before computing its tax, and owners who are 65 or older or disabled get a further $60,000 off. Each taxing unit may also adopt its own percentage exemption, up to 20 percent; the district office can tell you which Abilene units did.

School taxes on a home owned by someone 65 or older, or disabled, are also capped at the amount first qualified for. Disabled veterans receive exemptions of $5,000 to $12,000 based on a rating of 10 to 100 percent, and a veteran rated 100 percent can receive a total exemption on the residence homestead.

  • Apply with Taylor CAD by mail to P.O. Box 1800, by email to exemptions@cadtx.org, or in the drop box outside the district building.
  • There is no fee, and nobody needs to hire an agent.
  • The homestead exemption carries forward each year unless you move or the chief appraiser asks for a new application.
  • If the district has your birth date, the over-65 exemption is added automatically; otherwise call 325-676-9381.

The filing deadline for most exemptions is before May 1, and the district puts April 30 on nonprofit applications.

sections.h2: How do I protest an Abilene appraisal?
sections.html:
File a written protest with Taylor CAD. The Comptroller's calendar puts the cutoff at May 15, or 30 days after delivery of your value notice if that is later. Taylor CAD's FAQ speaks of May 31 instead, so treat the date on your notice as the one that counts. Notices start going out about April 1.

You can send the protest form by mail, email to arbprotest@cadtx.org, the drop box, or the district's online portal after setting up an account. The district first offers an informal meeting with an appraiser. If that fails, the appraisal review board hears the case at the district office, and you receive notice at least 15 days before the formal hearing.

Market value is the only thing you can protest, not the tax rate. A homestead's assessed value is held to 10 percent growth a year. If you lose before the board, the next steps are district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000.

sections.h2: What does Abilene look like for a seller with unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Abilene had 125,182 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 131,588 by July 2025, 5.3 percent above the 2020 base. The city covers 106.67 land square miles at 1,173.6 people per square mile. Among adults 25 and older, 87.7 percent finished high school and 27.3 percent went on to a bachelor's degree or more.

Owners occupy 56.1 percent of Abilene homes, leaving a large renter share. Over 2020 to 2024 the median value was $183,700 and the median gross rent $1,157. The typical commute is 15.6 minutes, and median household income is $62,648. City budget notes mention Rebuild ABI, funded at $1.5 million for affordable home renovation and construction, and a $19.3 million one-time sales tax surplus tied to data center construction.

A tax lien attaches to every Texas property on January 1 and secures that year's tax, penalties and interest. Whoever owned the house that day remains personally liable after selling, and title cannot be cleared until delinquent tax is paid. Before closing, request a payoff statement from Taylor CAD covering every year owed so the title company can settle it.

faqs.q: Does Abilene collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Central Appraisal District of Taylor County collects the bill for Taylor County properties, according to the Comptroller's county directory. The county tax office does not collect property tax.

faqs.q: What is Abilene's property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The city rate is 74.95 cents per $100 of taxable value, adopted September 10, 2026 for fiscal year 2027. The previous rate was 75.06 cents. Your total bill also includes the county, Abilene ISD and any other districts.

faqs.q: When do Abilene property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent on February 1 if unpaid on January 31. The collector adds a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest that day, and the penalty climbs to 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Can I get a tax break on my Abilene home?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. School district tax drops by a $140,000 homestead exemption, with $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Taylor CAD takes applications free of charge.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest an Abilene appraisal?
faqs.a: The state sets May 15, or 30 days after the notice arrives if later. Taylor CAD's FAQ lists May 31, so follow the date printed on your notice and file early.
